skills.name: Touch typing
skills.blurb: Type without looking at the keys, faster and with fewer mistakes.
skills.need: A computer keyboard. Type your drills right here in chat.
skills.safety: Sit tall, keep your wrists relaxed and level, and stop if anything aches.
warmups: Rest your fingers on the home keys (left hand on A S D F, right hand on J K L ;). Feel the small bumps on F and J. Lift your hands away and find the bumps again with your eyes closed, 10 times.
Without typing, tap each finger on its home key in turn, left little finger to right little finger and back, slowly, 5 rounds.
Shake out your hands, roll your shoulders, then type the alphabet once slowly without looking down.
Type your first name and the word 'ready' 5 times, eyes on the screen, not the keys.
skills.wrapup: Note your accuracy and which keys made you look down. Tomorrow, start with those keys.

stages.title: Home row
stages.goal: Type the home row keys without looking.

drills.title: Meet the home row
drills.do: Type each line of today's drill twice. Say each letter in your head as you press it. Accuracy matters more than speed today.

drills.title: Index finger stretch
drills.do: Your index fingers also cover G and H. Type today's lines, reaching sideways for G and H and coming straight back home.

drills.title: Little fingers
drills.do: Type today's lines, paying attention to A and L, the little-finger keys. Keep the other fingers resting lightly on home.

drills.title: Steady rhythm
drills.do: Type today's lines at an even beat, like a slow metronome. Same gap between every key, even the easy ones.

drills.title: Eyes up
drills.do: Cover your hands with a cloth or a sheet of paper. Type today's lines without peeking.

drills.title: Word flow
drills.do: Type today's lines as whole words, not single letters. Pause only at the spaces.

stages.easier: Type each line once, very slowly, and look at a key chart on screen instead of your hands.
stages.harder: Type each line three times and aim for no mistakes on the third try.

check.task: Set a 1-minute timer and type the check passage as far as you get. Paste what you typed in chat with the time you took.
check.record: words per minute and accuracy, worked out by your bot
check.ready_if: Accuracy of 90% or better without looking down.

stages.title: Top row reach, part 1
stages.goal: Add E, I, R and U to the home row.

drills.title: E and I
drills.do: E is your left middle finger reaching up; I is your right middle finger reaching up. Type today's lines and return each finger home after the reach.

drills.title: R and U
drills.do: R and U are the index fingers reaching up. Type today's lines, keeping your wrists still.

drills.title: Mixed reaches
drills.do: Type today's lines. When you miss a key, retype the whole word, not just the letter.

drills.title: Even beat
drills.do: Type today's lines at a steady beat, slow enough that you make no more than one mistake per line.

drills.title: Eyes up
drills.do: Cover your hands and type today's lines. Look only at the screen.

drills.title: Speed burst
drills.do: Type each of today's lines once slowly, then once a little faster. Notice where the faster try slips.

stages.easier: Practice just E and I today, and leave R and U for tomorrow.
stages.harder: Type each line with your eyes closed, then check it.

check.task: 1-minute timed test on the check passage. Paste your text and your time.

stages.title: Top row reach, part 2
stages.goal: Add T, Y, O, P, W and Q.

drills.title: T and Y
drills.do: T is a long reach up and to the right for the left index finger; Y is up and to the left for the right index finger. Type today's lines.

drills.title: O and P
drills.do: O is the right ring finger reaching up; P is the right little finger. Type today's lines.

drills.title: W and Q
drills.do: W is the left ring finger; Q is the left little finger. Type today's lines and keep the other fingers anchored.

drills.title: Whole top row
drills.do: Type today's lines. Then type q w e r t y u i o p three times without looking.

drills.title: Eyes up
drills.do: Cover your hands and type today's lines.

drills.title: Rhythm over speed
drills.do: Type today's lines at the fastest speed where you still make almost no mistakes.

stages.easier: Split the stage: T and Y today, the other four keys later this week.
stages.harder: Add a 1-minute speed burst at the end with the check passage.

check.task: 1-minute timed test on the check passage. Paste your text and your time.
check.ready_if: 90% accuracy and at least 15 words per minute.

stages.title: Bottom row
stages.goal: Add C, V, B, N, M, X and Z for the full alphabet.

drills.title: V, B, N and M
drills.do: The index fingers reach down: left for V and B, right for N and M. Type today's lines.

drills.title: C, X and Z
drills.do: C is the left middle finger, X the ring finger, Z the little finger, all reaching down. Type today's lines.

drills.title: Full alphabet
drills.do: Type today's lines. Then type the alphabet three times without looking.

drills.title: Tricky pairs
drills.do: Type today's lines, then pick the two letters you miss most and type 5 words with them.

drills.title: Eyes up
drills.do: Cover your hands and type today's lines.

drills.title: Longer run
drills.do: Type all of today's lines without stopping to fix mistakes. Then count your mistakes.

stages.easier: Practice only V, B, N and M today.
stages.harder: Type today's lines twice, the second time faster.

check.task: 1-minute timed test on the check passage. Paste your text and your time.
check.ready_if: 92% accuracy and at least 20 words per minute.

stages.title: Capitals, punctuation and numbers
stages.goal: Use Shift, common punctuation and the number row.

drills.title: Shift keys
drills.do: For a capital, hold Shift with the little finger of the opposite hand. Type today's lines.

drills.title: Period and comma
drills.do: Comma is the right middle finger reaching down; period is the right ring finger. Type today's lines.

drills.title: Question marks and apostrophes
drills.do: Type today's lines. The apostrophe and the question mark are both right little-finger keys.

drills.title: Number row
drills.do: Type today's lines with numbers. Reach up from the home row and come back each time.

drills.title: Eyes up
drills.do: Cover your hands and type today's lines.

drills.title: Mixed sentences
drills.do: Type today's lines at a steady pace and fix nothing until the end.

stages.easier: Skip the numbers this week and focus on capitals and periods.
stages.harder: Type each line, then retype it from memory.

check.task: 1-minute timed test on the check passage. Paste your text and your time.
check.ready_if: 92% accuracy and at least 22 words per minute.

stages.title: Speed and flow
stages.goal: Build speed on real sentences while keeping accuracy.

drills.title: Accuracy first
drills.do: Type today's lines with no mistakes at all. Slow down until that is easy.

drills.title: Speed bursts
drills.do: Type each line as fast as you can, then once at a comfortable pace. Compare the two.

drills.title: Copy from paper
drills.do: Copy a paragraph from any book or letter near you, eyes on the page, never on the keys.

drills.title: Write your own
drills.do: Type a short paragraph about your day without looking at the keys. Thinking and typing at once is the real skill.

drills.title: Weak keys
drills.do: Type today's lines, then 10 words that use your two weakest keys.

drills.title: Long run
drills.do: Type all of today's lines in one go, as a single 5-minute run.

stages.easier: Repeat the accuracy drill and skip the speed bursts.
stages.harder: Do two 1-minute tests and keep your best.

check.task: 1-minute timed test on the check passage. Paste your text and your time.
check.ready_if: 95% accuracy. Speed is your own target from here.

skills.name: Drawing basics
skills.blurb: Learn to see and draw lines, shapes, shading and simple scenes.
skills.need: A pencil (an ordinary one is fine), an eraser and plain paper.
warmups: Fill a quarter page with straight lines, drawing from your shoulder, not your wrist. Go slowly, then a little faster.
Draw 20 circles and 20 ovals of different sizes. Go around each one twice lightly before you commit.
Draw 10 straight lines between pairs of dots you place yourself. Aim to hit each dot.
Shade a small box from light to dark in one smooth sweep, three times.
skills.wrapup: Write the date on today's page. Snap a photo if you like, so you can compare later.

resources.label: The Practice and Science of Drawing (full book, free)

stages.title: Lines and seeing
stages.goal: Control your pencil and draw what you see, not what you think you see.

drills.title: Before drawing
drills.do: Draw your own hand, or a mug, for 10 minutes. Keep it. You will draw it again at the end of the plan.

drills.title: Blind contour
drills.do: Look only at your hand and draw its outline slowly without looking at the paper. It will look odd; that is the point.

drills.title: Contour
drills.do: Draw a shoe or a cup with one slow continuous line, glancing at the paper only now and then.

drills.title: Straight and curved
drills.do: Draw a still life of three simple objects using only straight lines, then again using only curves.

drills.title: Upside down
drills.do: Turn a photo upside down and copy it. You will draw shapes and angles instead of labels.

drills.title: Slow line
drills.do: Pick one object and draw its edge as slowly as you can, matching your eye to your pencil.

stages.easier: Use bigger paper and draw only one object per session.
stages.harder: Add the inside edges too: folds, seams and the borders of shadows.

check.task: Draw a mug from life for 8 minutes.
check.record: a photo or a note on what got easier
check.ready_if: You looked at the mug more than at the paper.

stages.title: Shapes and proportion
stages.goal: Build objects from simple shapes and measure with your pencil.

drills.title: Shape breakdown
drills.do: Look at three objects and draw each as circles, boxes and triangles before adding detail.

drills.title: Pencil measuring
drills.do: Hold your pencil at arm's length and compare an object's height to its width. Draw it to match.

drills.title: Negative space
drills.do: Draw a chair by drawing only the empty shapes between its legs and rungs.

drills.title: Ellipses
drills.do: Draw cups, bowls and jar lids. Notice how a circle looks flatter the lower you view it.

drills.title: Boxes
drills.do: Draw 10 boxes from different angles, including a cereal box from life.

drills.title: Small still life
drills.do: Set up three objects and draw them with correct sizes relative to each other.

stages.easier: Draw single objects only, no groups.
stages.harder: Draw the group from two different viewpoints.

check.task: Draw a small still life of three objects for 10 minutes.
check.ready_if: The sizes look right next to each other.

stages.title: Light and shading
stages.goal: Show light and form with values from light to dark.

drills.title: Value scale
drills.do: Draw a strip of 5 boxes and shade them from white to your darkest dark in even steps.

drills.title: Hatching
drills.do: Shade with parallel lines, then cross-hatching. Make a value scale with lines only.

drills.title: Shaded ball
drills.do: Draw a sphere lit from one side: highlight, light, shadow side, cast shadow.

drills.title: Shaded cube and cylinder
drills.do: Shade a box and a can with the light from the same direction.

drills.title: Squint
drills.do: Squint at a real object to see its big light and dark areas. Shade only those, no detail.

drills.title: Egg study
drills.do: Place an egg or a ball near a lamp and draw it with full shading.

stages.easier: Use three values only: light, middle and dark.
stages.harder: Add reflected light on the shadow side.

check.task: Draw and shade one object near a lamp for 10 minutes.
check.ready_if: It looks round or solid, not flat.

stages.title: Perspective
stages.goal: Draw space and depth with one-point and two-point perspective.

drills.title: One-point boxes
drills.do: Draw a horizon line and one dot on it. Draw 6 boxes with their sides heading to the dot.

drills.title: A hallway
drills.do: Draw a hallway or road in one-point perspective with doors or posts.

drills.title: Two-point boxes
drills.do: Put two dots far apart on the horizon. Draw boxes with edges heading to both.

drills.title: A building corner
drills.do: Draw the corner of a house or a room in two-point perspective.

drills.title: Room from life
drills.do: Sit in a corner and draw the room. Find the horizon at your eye level first.

drills.title: Objects in space
drills.do: Draw three objects on a table, smaller and higher on the page as they go back.

stages.easier: Stay with one-point perspective all week.
stages.harder: Add a door that is half open.

check.task: Draw a street, hallway or room in perspective for 10 minutes.
check.ready_if: Lines that should meet do meet at your dots.

stages.title: Gesture and people
stages.goal: Draw quick, lively figures and simple proportions.

drills.title: 30-second gestures
drills.do: Draw a person (a photo, a paused video, or someone nearby) in 30 seconds, catching the main curve of the pose. Do 15.

drills.title: Stick and bean
drills.do: Draw figures as a line of action plus a bean shape for the body. Do 10 poses.

drills.title: Heads
drills.do: Draw an oval head and place the eyes about halfway down. Draw 6 heads facing different ways.

drills.title: Hands again
drills.do: Draw your hand in three poses, as shapes first, then contour.

drills.title: Longer pose
drills.do: Draw one figure for 10 minutes: gesture first, then shapes, then contour.

drills.title: People out and about
drills.do: Sketch people in a cafe, a park or on TV with quick gestures.

stages.easier: Use 1-minute poses instead of 30 seconds.
stages.harder: Do 15-second poses and add a 5-minute pose at the end.

check.task: Ten 30-second gestures, then one 5-minute figure.
check.ready_if: Your figures show movement, not just stiff outlines.

stages.title: Putting it together
stages.goal: Combine line, proportion, shading and space in finished drawings.

drills.title: Plan a drawing
drills.do: Pick a subject, make three tiny thumbnail sketches and choose the best layout.

drills.title: Still life, part 1
drills.do: Draw your chosen still life with shapes and proportion.

drills.title: Still life, part 2
drills.do: Shade the same drawing with a clear light direction.

drills.title: A view
drills.do: Draw a view from a window or outdoors with a near, middle and far part.

drills.title: Portrait from a photo
drills.do: Draw a face from a photo, measuring with your pencil.

drills.title: Free choice
drills.do: Draw anything you love for 10 minutes, using what you have learned.

stages.easier: Spread one finished drawing across two sessions.
stages.harder: Work from life only, no photos.

check.task: Draw the same subject as your first session (your hand or the mug) for 10 minutes. Put the two side by side.
check.record: a photo or a note on what changed
check.ready_if: You can point to at least three things you now do differently.

skills.name: Chess
skills.blurb: Learn the rules, the basic checkmates, simple tactics and a sound plan for the opening.
skills.need: A chess set, or a free online board.
warmups: Set up the board from memory: a light square in each player's right-hand corner, the queen on her own color.
Name every square a knight can reach from g1, then from e4.
Solve two easy puzzles on a free puzzle board, or replay the last game you played.
Say how each piece moves, out loud, in under a minute.
skills.wrapup: Write one thing you learned today in a sentence.

stages.title: The pieces and the rules
stages.goal: Know how every piece moves and the special rules.

drills.title: Rooks and bishops
drills.do: Rooks move along ranks and files; bishops move diagonally. Place one on a board and list every square it can reach. Then try with pieces in the way.

drills.title: Queen, king and knight
drills.do: The queen moves like a rook or a bishop; the king moves one square in any direction; the knight moves in an L and can jump. Move each around an empty board.

drills.title: Pawns
drills.do: Pawns move forward one square, or two from their starting square, and capture one square diagonally forward. Play a pawns-only game: first pawn to the far side wins.

drills.title: Check and checkmate
drills.do: Set up 5 positions where a king is in check and find every way out: move, block or capture. Then set up one checkmate.

drills.title: Castling and promotion
drills.do: Practice castling on both sides. You may not castle out of, through or into check, or if the king or that rook has moved. Promote a pawn to a queen.

drills.title: En passant and draws
drills.do: Set up an en passant capture. Then read about stalemate, threefold repetition and the 50-move rule in the official Laws.

stages.easier: Learn one piece per session.
stages.harder: Play one full slow game against a friend or a computer at its easiest level.

check.task: Play a full game and make only legal moves, including one castle.

stages.title: Basic checkmates
stages.goal: Checkmate a lone king with a queen, and with a rook.

drills.title: Queen and king
drills.do: Set up your king and queen against a lone king. Use the queen to herd the king to the edge, then bring your king up and mate. Watch out for stalemate.

drills.title: Queen mate again
drills.do: Repeat the queen mate from three different starting positions.

drills.title: Rook and king
drills.do: Use the rook to cut the king off rank by rank, with your king's help, until it is on the edge. Then mate.

drills.title: Rook mate again
drills.do: Repeat the rook mate from three different starting positions. Count your moves.

drills.title: Back-rank mate
drills.do: Set up a king stuck behind its own pawns and mate it with a rook on the back rank. Then see how a pawn move made earlier would have prevented it.

drills.title: Checkmate practice
drills.do: Open the free practice lessons and do the checkmate section.

stages.easier: Stick to the queen mate this week.
stages.harder: Mate with two rooks, then with a queen against a king and pawn.

check.task: Mate a lone king with king and rook from a random start.
check.ready_if: Checkmate within 30 moves, with no stalemate.

stages.title: Opening principles
stages.goal: Start games with a sound plan.

drills.title: Control the center
drills.do: Play 5 openings where your first moves put pawns on e4 or d4 (e5 or d5 as Black).

drills.title: Develop pieces
drills.do: Bring out knights and bishops before moving the same piece twice. Play the first 8 moves of 3 games this way.

drills.title: Castle early
drills.do: Play 3 openings where you castle within the first 10 moves.

drills.title: Don't hang pieces
drills.do: Before each move, ask: what does my move leave unprotected, and what is my opponent threatening?

drills.title: Study a model game
drills.do: Play through one short example from the free book on a board.

drills.title: Play
drills.do: Play one game, slowly, focusing only on the opening principles.

stages.easier: Play only the first 10 moves of games.
stages.harder: Play two games and write down your first 10 moves of each.

check.task: Play a game and review its first 10 moves.
check.record: how many opening principles you followed
check.ready_if: Center, development and castling all done by move 10.

stages.title: Tactics
stages.goal: Spot forks, pins, skewers and discovered attacks.

drills.title: Forks
drills.do: A fork attacks two pieces at once. Solve 5 fork puzzles from the puzzles by theme.

drills.title: Pins
drills.do: A pin stops a piece from moving without exposing a more valuable piece behind it. Solve 5 pin puzzles.

drills.title: Skewers
drills.do: A skewer attacks a valuable piece that must move, exposing a piece behind it. Solve 5 skewer puzzles.

drills.title: Discovered attacks
drills.do: Moving one piece uncovers an attack by another. Solve 5 discovered attack puzzles.

drills.title: Mixed puzzles
drills.do: Solve 10 mixed puzzles. Before each move, look at every check, capture and threat.

drills.title: Play and spot
drills.do: Play one game and look for one tactic per move, for you and your opponent.

stages.easier: Solve 3 puzzles per session instead of 5.
stages.harder: Solve puzzles without moving the pieces until you are sure.

check.task: Solve 10 mixed puzzles.
check.record: how many you solved on the first try

stages.title: Endgames
stages.goal: Win and hold simple king and pawn endings.

drills.title: King activity
drills.do: In the endgame the king becomes a fighter. Play out king and pawn against king from 5 positions.

drills.title: The square of the pawn
drills.do: Picture a square from the pawn to its promotion rank. If the defending king can step into it, it catches the pawn. Test the rule on 5 positions.

drills.title: Opposition
drills.do: When the kings face each other with one square between them, the side that just moved has the opposition. Practice it in king and pawn endings.

drills.title: Rook endings
drills.do: Rooks belong behind passed pawns. Play out 3 rook and pawn positions.

drills.title: Endgame lessons
drills.do: Do the pawn endgame section of the free practice lessons.

drills.title: Study from the book
drills.do: Play through the first endgame examples of the free book.

stages.easier: Practice only king and pawn against king.
stages.harder: Play each position as both sides.

check.task: Win king and pawn against king from 3 winning positions.

stages.title: Playing and learning from games
stages.goal: Play full games and learn from your own mistakes.

drills.title: Slow game
drills.do: Play one slow game. Write down your moves.

drills.title: Review
drills.do: Replay your last game on the free analysis board. Find your biggest mistake.

drills.title: Threat check
drills.do: Play a game where before every move you name your opponent's threat.

drills.title: Middle game plans
drills.do: Play a game and, after the opening, pick one weak point to aim at.

drills.title: Puzzle rush
drills.do: Solve as many puzzles as you can in 10 minutes.

drills.title: Review again
drills.do: Review one more of your games and write down the lesson in one sentence.

stages.easier: Play shorter games and review just one moment.
stages.harder: Review every capture in your game, not only the big mistake.

check.task: Play a full game, then review it.
check.ready_if: You found at least one mistake and a better move.

skills.name: Spreadsheets
skills.blurb: Formulas, sorting, lookups, charts and pivot tables in any common spreadsheet app.
skills.need: Any spreadsheet app: Google Sheets, Excel or LibreOffice Calc. Each day's practice table is made for you in chat.
warmups: Paste today's practice table into a new sheet. Make the header row bold.
Move around with only the keyboard: arrow keys, Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) plus an arrow to jump to the edge, Shift plus arrows to select.
Select the Units column and read its total in the status bar at the bottom of the window.
Undo, redo, copy and paste five times using only keyboard shortcuts.
skills.wrapup: Reply with your answers. Your bot checks them against the right values.

stages.title: Cells and simple formulas
stages.goal: Enter data and use SUM, AVERAGE, MIN and MAX.

drills.title: Cells and ranges
drills.do: Paste today's table. Click cells and read their addresses, like B3. Select the Units numbers and see their sum in the status bar.

drills.title: SUM
drills.do: Under the Units column, type =SUM( and select the numbers. Press Enter. Answer today's questions.

drills.title: AVERAGE, MIN, MAX
drills.do: Use =AVERAGE, =MIN and =MAX on today's columns. Answer today's questions.

drills.title: Simple math
drills.do: Add a Revenue column with =D2*E2 (units times price) and fill it down by dragging the small square at the cell's corner.

drills.title: Fill a series
drills.do: Type 1 and 2 in two cells, select both and drag down to make 1 to 20. Try it with Jan and Feb too.

drills.title: Put it together
drills.do: Make a small summary block: total units, average price, biggest sale. Answer today's questions.

stages.easier: Use the AutoSum button instead of typing formulas.
stages.harder: Write every formula by typing, no buttons.

check.task: Answer today's practice questions using formulas only.

stages.title: Formatting, sorting and filtering
stages.goal: Make tables readable and find what you need fast.

drills.title: Number formats
drills.do: Format prices as currency and add a Revenue column formatted with two decimals.

drills.title: Sort
drills.do: Sort the table by Units from largest to smallest. Then by Region, then by Item.

drills.title: Filter
drills.do: Turn on a filter and show only one region. Answer today's questions.

drills.title: Freeze the header
drills.do: Freeze the top row so it stays visible when you scroll.

drills.title: Absolute references
drills.do: Put a tax rate in a cell, like 0.08 in H1. Write =F2*$H$1 next to your Revenue column and fill it down. See why the dollar signs matter.

drills.title: Tidy table
drills.do: Make today's table look finished: bold headers, borders, aligned numbers.

stages.easier: Sort only; leave filters for next week.
stages.harder: Sort by two columns at once.

check.task: Answer today's practice questions with sort and filter.

stages.title: IF, COUNTIF and SUMIF
stages.goal: Make formulas that decide and count.

drills.title: IF
drills.do: Add a column with =IF(D2>=50,"Big","Small") and fill it down.

drills.title: COUNTIF
drills.do: Count rows for one region with =COUNTIF(C2:C13,"North"). Answer today's questions.

drills.title: SUMIF
drills.do: Total the units for one region with =SUMIF(C2:C13,"North",D2:D13).

drills.title: Conditions with numbers
drills.do: Count rows with more than 50 units with =COUNTIF(D2:D13,">50").

drills.title: Combine
drills.do: Make a small table of each region with its row count and total units.

drills.title: Check yourself
drills.do: Answer today's questions, then check one answer with a filter instead.

stages.easier: Use only COUNTIF this week.
stages.harder: Try COUNTIFS and SUMIFS with two conditions.

check.task: Answer today's practice questions with formulas.

stages.title: Lookups
stages.goal: Pull values from another table.

drills.title: Two tables
drills.do: Paste today's sales table and its price list side by side.

drills.title: VLOOKUP
drills.do: Look up a price with =VLOOKUP(item, price list range, 2, FALSE). FALSE means an exact match.

drills.title: INDEX and MATCH
drills.do: Do the same lookup with =INDEX(price column, MATCH(item, item column, 0)).

drills.title: Missing values
drills.do: Look up an item that isn't in the list, then wrap the formula in IFERROR to show 'Not found'.

drills.title: XLOOKUP if you have it
drills.do: If your app has XLOOKUP, repeat the lookup with it. If not, repeat INDEX and MATCH.

drills.title: Answer questions
drills.do: Answer today's questions using lookups.

stages.easier: Use VLOOKUP only.
stages.harder: Look up from a table on another sheet tab.

check.task: Answer today's lookup questions.

stages.title: Charts and clean data
stages.goal: Show data visually and keep it clean.

drills.title: A column chart
drills.do: Chart units by item as a column chart. Give it a clear title.

drills.title: A line chart
drills.do: Make a line chart of units by month from today's table.

drills.title: Conditional formatting
drills.do: Color Units cells over 50 green and under 20 red.

drills.title: Data validation
drills.do: Make the Region column a drop-down list of the four regions.

drills.title: Text clean-up
drills.do: Use TRIM, UPPER and PROPER on messy text, and join text with &.

drills.title: Mini dashboard
drills.do: Build two charts and a summary block on one sheet.

stages.easier: Make one chart per session.
stages.harder: Add a chart that updates when you filter.

check.task: Chart total units by region and answer today's questions.
check.ready_if: All correct and the chart is readable.

stages.title: Pivot tables and a mini project
stages.goal: Summarize data fast and finish a real sheet.

drills.title: First pivot table
drills.do: Insert a pivot table with Region as rows and the sum of Units as values.

drills.title: Pivot by two fields
drills.do: Add Item as columns. Read off which region sold the most of one item.

drills.title: Dates
drills.do: Use =TODAY() and subtract dates to count the days since each order.

drills.title: Plan your own sheet
drills.do: Pick a real use: a budget, a habit tracker or a reading log. Sketch its columns.

drills.title: Build it
drills.do: Build your sheet with at least one SUMIF, one lookup or one chart.

drills.title: Finish it
drills.do: Polish your sheet: formats, a frozen header and a chart.

stages.easier: Use the practice table for your project.
stages.harder: Add a pivot chart to your project.

check.task: Answer today's questions using a pivot table.

skills.name: Public speaking
skills.blurb: Speak clearly and calmly, with a simple structure and fewer filler words.
skills.need: Your phone's voice or video recorder and a quiet spot.
warmups: Breathe in for 4 counts and out for 6, five times. Let your shoulders drop.
Hum for 30 seconds, then say 'red leather, yellow leather' slowly 5 times, then faster.
Stand tall with your weight on both feet. Say today's topic out loud to an empty room.
Read any paragraph aloud slowly, pausing at every period for a full breath.
skills.wrapup: Play back your recording. Count your filler words (um, uh, like, you know) and tell me the count and your talk length.

resources.label: The Art of Public Speaking (full book, free)

stages.title: Voice, breath and presence
stages.goal: Speak for one minute calmly and audibly.

drills.title: Baseline
drills.do: Record yourself talking about today's topic for 1 minute, with no preparation. Keep this recording.

drills.title: Breath
drills.do: Talk about today's topic in short sentences, breathing at each period. Record 1 minute.

drills.title: Volume
drills.do: Speak to the far wall of the room, not to someone beside you. Record 1 minute.

drills.title: Posture
drills.do: Record a 1-minute video. Feet planted, hands still or open, eyes up.

drills.title: Pauses
drills.do: Replace every 'um' with a silent pause. Record 1 minute.

drills.title: Slow down
drills.do: Record 1 minute at what feels slightly too slow. Play it back and notice how it sounds.

stages.easier: Record 30 seconds instead of a minute.
stages.harder: Record 2 minutes.

check.task: Record 1 minute on today's topic.
check.ready_if: Fewer filler words than your baseline.

stages.title: Structure
stages.goal: Use an opening, three points and a close.

drills.title: Three points
drills.do: Write three short points on today's topic. Record a talk that covers each in order.

drills.title: Strong opening
drills.do: Open with a question, a true fact you know well, or a short scene. Record the first 30 seconds three ways.

drills.title: Clear close
drills.do: End with one sentence that sums up and one thing to do. Record 1 minute that ends strongly.

drills.title: Signposts
drills.do: Use words like 'first', 'next' and 'finally'. Record a 2-minute talk.

drills.title: Notes on one card
drills.do: Put only 5 keywords on a card. Give a 2-minute talk from it.

drills.title: Full run
drills.do: Give a 2-minute structured talk on today's topic.

stages.easier: Use two points instead of three.
stages.harder: Give the talk with no notes.

check.task: Record a 2-minute talk with an opening, three points and a close.
check.ready_if: All parts present and within 20 seconds of 2 minutes.

stages.title: Stories
stages.goal: Tell a short true story that holds attention.

drills.title: Pick a story
drills.do: Write down three short moments from your own life. Pick one.

drills.title: Shape
drills.do: Tell the story as: where and when, what went wrong, what you did, what changed. Record it.

drills.title: Details
drills.do: Add one detail for each sense you can. Record it again.

drills.title: Dialogue
drills.do: Retell it with one line someone actually said. Record it.

drills.title: Cut it down
drills.do: Tell the same story in 60 seconds.

drills.title: A story with a point
drills.do: Tell the story, then one sentence about what it means. Record it.

stages.easier: Tell the story to a friend instead of recording it.
stages.harder: Tell it standing up, on video, with no notes.

check.task: Record a 2-minute true story.
check.ready_if: It has a clear start, problem and change.

stages.title: Explaining clearly
stages.goal: Explain a process so a beginner can follow.

drills.title: One idea
drills.do: Explain today's topic to an imagined 12-year-old in 1 minute.

drills.title: Steps
drills.do: Explain how to do something you know well, in 5 steps. Record it.

drills.title: An example
drills.do: Add one concrete example to your last explanation.

drills.title: Show it
drills.do: Explain something while showing it with an object or a sketch.

drills.title: Check understanding
drills.do: Give your explanation to someone and ask them to repeat it back.

drills.title: Full run
drills.do: Give a 3-minute how-to talk.

stages.easier: Use 3 steps instead of 5.
stages.harder: Explain without any jargon at all.

check.task: Record a 3-minute how-to talk.

stages.title: Persuading
stages.goal: Make a clear case and ask for something.

drills.title: One-sentence case
drills.do: Write your position on today's topic in one sentence. Say it out loud 5 ways.

drills.title: Reasons
drills.do: Give three reasons, the strongest last. Record it.

drills.title: The other side
drills.do: Name the best argument against you and answer it fairly. Record it.

drills.title: The ask
drills.do: End with a specific request. Record 1 minute.

drills.title: Emphasis
drills.do: Mark the three most important words in your talk and lean on them.

drills.title: Full run
drills.do: Give a 3-minute persuasive talk.

stages.easier: Persuade on something low-stakes, like a favorite food.
stages.harder: Argue for the side you disagree with.

check.task: Record a 3-minute persuasive talk.
check.ready_if: It has a clear position, reasons and an ask.

stages.title: Speaking on your feet
stages.goal: Answer unexpected questions and give a full talk.

drills.title: Impromptu
drills.do: Take today's topic as a surprise: 10 seconds to think, then speak for 1 minute.

drills.title: Answer framework
drills.do: Answer today's topic with: point, reason, example, point. 1 minute.

drills.title: Q and A
drills.do: Write 5 questions someone might ask after one of your talks. Answer each in 30 seconds.

drills.title: Recover
drills.do: Practice losing your place: pause, breathe, repeat your last point, carry on.

drills.title: Prepare a 5-minute talk
drills.do: Outline a 5-minute talk on a topic you care about.

drills.title: Rehearse
drills.do: Rehearse your 5-minute talk twice, recording the second run.

stages.easier: Take 30 seconds to prepare before each impromptu answer.
stages.harder: Ask someone else to pick your surprise topics.

check.task: Record your 5-minute talk and compare it with your first baseline recording.
check.record: length, filler words and what changed
check.ready_if: Fewer filler words than your first recording.

skills.name: Mental math
skills.blurb: Add, subtract, multiply and work out percentages in your head, quickly and accurately.
skills.need: Nothing but chat. Each day's problems are made fresh and checked by your bot.
warmups: Count up by 7 from 0 to 70, then back down.
Make 100: say the partner of 37, 64, 18, 81 and 45.
Double these quickly: 16, 35, 48, 125.
Halve these quickly: 74, 130, 58, 312.
skills.wrapup: Reply with your answers in order, separated by commas, and roughly how long you took.

stages.title: Adding left to right
stages.goal: Add two-digit numbers in your head.

drills.title: Tens first
drills.do: Add the tens, then the ones. 47 + 38: 70, then 15, so 85. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Make a ten
drills.do: Shift a little to make a round number: 48 + 27 is 50 + 25. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Out loud
drills.do: Say each step aloud as you solve today's set.

drills.title: Speed round
drills.do: Solve today's set as fast as you can, then redo your slowest one.

drills.title: Chains
drills.do: Solve today's set, then add your first three answers together.

drills.title: Mixed
drills.do: Solve today's set using whichever trick fits each problem.

stages.easier: Use smaller numbers: one-digit plus two-digit.
stages.harder: Use three-digit plus two-digit numbers.

check.task: Solve the 10-problem check set.

stages.title: Subtracting and partners to 100
stages.goal: Subtract fast and find partners to 100.

drills.title: Partners to 100
drills.do: For 37 the partner is 63: the tens add to 9 and the ones add to 10. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Count up
drills.do: For 82 - 47, count up from 47: 3 to get to 50, 32 more to 82, so 35. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Round and fix
drills.do: 73 - 28 is 73 - 30, plus 2. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Speed round
drills.do: Solve today's set as fast as you can.

drills.title: Making change
drills.do: Treat each problem as making change from a bill. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Mixed
drills.do: Solve today's set with any trick.

stages.easier: Subtract one-digit numbers from two-digit numbers.
stages.harder: Subtract two-digit numbers from three-digit numbers.

check.task: Solve the 10-problem check set.

stages.title: Shortcuts: times 5, 11 and 25
stages.goal: Multiply by 5, 11 and 25 in a blink.

drills.title: Times 5
drills.do: Times 5 is times 10, then halve. 48 x 5: 480, half is 240. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Times 11
drills.do: For a two-digit number, put the sum of its digits in the middle: 43 x 11 is 4, 7, 3, so 473. If the sum is 10 or more, carry the 1: 68 x 11 is 748.

drills.title: Times 25
drills.do: Times 25 is times 100, then divide by 4. 36 x 25: 3600 divided by 4 is 900.

drills.title: Mixed shortcuts
drills.do: Solve today's set, naming the trick before you start each problem.

drills.title: Speed round
drills.do: Solve today's set as fast as you can.

drills.title: Explain it
drills.do: Solve today's set, then explain in one sentence why one of the tricks works.

stages.easier: Practice only times 5.
stages.harder: Use three-digit numbers.

check.task: Solve the 10-problem check set.

stages.title: Two-digit times one-digit
stages.goal: Multiply by splitting numbers apart.

drills.title: Split
drills.do: 67 x 4 is 60 x 4 plus 7 x 4: 240 + 28 = 268. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Double and halve
drills.do: Double one number and halve the other: 16 x 35 is 8 x 70, which is 560. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Round and fix
drills.do: 49 x 6 is 50 x 6, minus 6: 294. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Speed round
drills.do: Solve today's set as fast as you can.

drills.title: Out loud
drills.do: Say each step aloud while you solve.

drills.title: Mixed
drills.do: Solve today's set using any trick.

stages.easier: Keep the one-digit number at 2, 3 or 4.
stages.harder: Try two-digit times two-digit problems.

check.task: Solve the 10-problem check set.

stages.title: Squares and percentages
stages.goal: Square numbers and find common percentages.

drills.title: Squares ending in 5
drills.do: For 35 squared: 3 x 4 = 12, then write 25 after it, so 1225. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Squares near a round number
drills.do: For 23 squared: 20 x 26 + 3 x 3 = 520 + 9 = 529. Solve today's set.

drills.title: 10 percent
drills.do: 10% moves the decimal point one place left. 10% of 340 is 34. Solve today's set.

drills.title: 15 and 20 percent
drills.do: 15% is 10% plus half of that. 20% is 10% doubled. Solve today's set.

drills.title: Speed round
drills.do: Solve today's set as fast as you can.

drills.title: Mixed
drills.do: Solve today's set using any trick.

stages.easier: Practice 10% and 20% only.
stages.harder: Square numbers from 31 to 60.

check.task: Solve the 10-problem check set.

stages.title: Mixed and estimating
stages.goal: Pick the right trick fast and estimate sensibly.

drills.title: Mixed set
drills.do: Solve today's set, naming the trick first.

drills.title: Estimate first
drills.do: Before solving each problem, say a rough answer. Then solve and compare.

drills.title: Speed round
drills.do: Solve today's set as fast as you can.

drills.title: Out loud
drills.do: Explain each step aloud.

drills.title: Everyday math
drills.do: Solve today's set, then work out a real tip or a split bill in your head.

drills.title: Personal best
drills.do: Solve today's set and try to beat your best time.

stages.easier: Take as long as you need; accuracy only.
stages.harder: Give yourself 2 minutes for the whole set.

check.task: Solve the 10-problem check set.

skills.name: Knots
skills.blurb: Tie a set of useful knots, hitches and bends, then tie them without looking.
skills.need: Two pieces of soft rope or cord about an arm's length each, ideally of different thicknesses, and a broom handle or chair leg for hitches.
skills.safety: These sessions are for learning to tie knots. Never trust a knot from this plan to hold a person, a climber, a boat in bad weather or anything that could fall on someone. For those, learn from a qualified instructor.

measure.name: Knots you can tie without looking

warmups: Tie and untie an overhand knot 5 times with each hand leading.
Tie the last knot you learned 3 times, then once with your eyes closed.
Name the parts of the rope: the working end (the end you tie with), the standing part (the rest) and a bight (a U-shaped fold).
Tie each knot from your last session once, slowly.
skills.wrapup: Tell me which knots you can now tie without looking.

resources.label: Knots, Splices and Rope Work (full book, free)

stages.title: Stoppers and the square knot
stages.goal: Tie the overhand, figure-eight, slip knot and square knot.

drills.title: Overhand knot
drills.do: Make a loop and pass the working end through it. It is the simplest knot and the start of many others.

drills.title: Figure-eight knot
drills.do: Make a loop, take the end around behind the standing part, then down through the loop. It stops a rope sliding through a hole and is easier to untie than an overhand.

drills.title: Slip knot
drills.do: Tie an overhand knot around a bight of the rope instead of the end, so that pulling the end releases it.

drills.title: Square knot
drills.do: Right over left and under, then left over right and under. It ties the two ends of one cord around something, like a parcel or a bandage. Never use it to join two ropes that will take a load: it can slip or spill.

drills.title: Granny check
drills.do: Tie a granny knot (right over left twice) next to a square knot. Learn to see the difference.

drills.title: Review
drills.do: Tie all four knots three times each, then each once without looking.

stages.easier: Learn two knots this week.
stages.harder: Tie each knot behind your back.

check.task: Tie the four knots without looking.

stages.title: Bends and the bowline
stages.goal: Join two ropes and tie a fixed loop.

drills.title: Sheet bend
drills.do: Make a bight in the thicker rope. Pass the thinner end up through it, around behind both legs of the bight, and tuck it under itself.

drills.title: Double sheet bend
drills.do: Tie a sheet bend, but take the end around behind the bight a second time before the tuck.

drills.title: Bowline
drills.do: Make a small loop in the standing part. Bring the end up through it, around behind the standing part, and back down through the small loop. Tighten.

drills.title: Bowline around a post
drills.do: Tie a bowline around a chair leg, as you would around a post.

drills.title: Check your bowline
drills.do: Look at it: the end should finish inside the loop. Tie it 5 times.

drills.title: Review
drills.do: Tie the sheet bend and bowline three times each, then once without looking.

stages.easier: Focus on the bowline only.
stages.harder: Tie the bowline with your eyes closed.

check.task: Tie a sheet bend and a bowline without looking.

stages.title: Hitches
stages.goal: Tie a rope to a post or ring.

drills.title: Clove hitch
drills.do: Wrap the rope around a post, cross over the first turn, wrap again and tuck the end under the second turn.

drills.title: Round turn and two half hitches
drills.do: Take two turns around a post, then tie two half hitches around the standing part.

drills.title: Timber hitch
drills.do: Pass the rope around a pole, around the standing part, then twist the end back around itself three times.

drills.title: Clove hitch over a post
drills.do: Tie the clove hitch by making two loops in your hands and dropping them over the end of a post.

drills.title: Which hitch?
drills.do: For three jobs (a leash to a post, a pole to drag, a clothesline) pick a hitch and tie it.

drills.title: Review
drills.do: Tie all three hitches three times each, then once without looking.

stages.easier: Learn the clove hitch and the round turn only.
stages.harder: Tie each hitch in under 10 seconds.

check.task: Tie the three hitches without looking.

stages.title: Adjustable and tensioning knots
stages.goal: Tighten a line and tie off to a cleat.

drills.title: Taut-line hitch
drills.do: Pass the rope around a post. Take two turns around the standing part inside the loop, then one more turn further along the standing part, and tuck. It slides to adjust and grips under load.

drills.title: Trucker's hitch
drills.do: Follow the diagram: make a loop in the standing part, pass the end around an anchor and back through the loop, pull tight and finish with two half hitches.

drills.title: Cleat hitch
drills.do: Follow the diagram: a turn around the base of the cleat, a figure-eight over its horns, and a locking turn.

drills.title: Practice line
drills.do: Run a line between two chairs with a taut-line hitch. Slide it tighter and looser.

drills.title: Speed
drills.do: Time yourself tying each knot from this week.

drills.title: Review
drills.do: Tie every knot from this week three times, then once without looking.

stages.easier: Learn the taut-line hitch only.
stages.harder: Tie the trucker's hitch with your eyes closed.

check.task: Tie the three knots without looking.

stages.title: Grip knots and loops
stages.goal: Tie the constrictor, double fisherman's and alpine butterfly.

drills.title: Constrictor knot
drills.do: Tie it like a clove hitch, then tuck the end under the crossing so it grips hard. Good for closing a bag.

drills.title: Double fisherman's
drills.do: Lay two ends side by side. Each end ties a double overhand knot around the other rope. Pull the two knots together.

drills.title: Alpine butterfly
drills.do: Follow the diagram step by step to make a loop in the middle of a rope.

drills.title: Compare loops
drills.do: Tie a bowline and an alpine butterfly. Say when you would pick each.

drills.title: Speed
drills.do: Time yourself tying each knot from this week.

drills.title: Review
drills.do: Tie every knot from this week three times, then once without looking.

stages.easier: Learn the constrictor and the double fisherman's only.
stages.harder: Tie each knot in under 15 seconds.

check.task: Tie the three knots without looking.

stages.title: Mastery
stages.goal: Tie every knot from memory and pick the right one for the job.

drills.title: Prusik
drills.do: Follow the diagram to tie a loop of thin cord around a thicker rope so it grips. Slide it, then pull on it.

drills.title: Eyes closed round
drills.do: Tie every knot from the plan with your eyes closed.

drills.title: Job match
drills.do: For 6 everyday jobs (a parcel, a hammock, a tarp, a tow line, a boat to a dock, a bag) pick a knot and tie it.

drills.title: Speed round
drills.do: Tie all your knots as fast as you can. Note your total time.

drills.title: Untie test
drills.do: Pull each knot hard, then untie it. Note which ones jam.

drills.title: Teach it
drills.do: Teach one knot to someone, or explain it out loud step by step.

stages.easier: Focus on your five favorite knots.
stages.harder: Tie every knot you can with one hand.

check.task: Tie every knot from the plan without looking.
check.ready_if: All of them, or all but one.

skills.name: Juggling
skills.blurb: Go from one ball to a steady three-ball cascade, then a few tricks.
skills.need: Three soft balls of the same size: beanbags, tennis balls or rolled-up socks.
skills.safety: Clear the space around you, away from anything breakable. Standing in front of a bed saves a lot of bending down.
warmups: Roll your shoulders and wrists for 30 seconds.
Toss one ball from hand to hand 20 times in an arc that peaks just above eye level.
Toss one ball 10 times with each hand, catching in the same hand.
Stand tall, elbows at your sides, forearms forward. That is your home position.
skills.wrapup: Tell me your best run today.

stages.title: One ball
stages.goal: A steady, even throw from hand to hand.

drills.title: The arc
drills.do: Toss one ball from hand to hand in an arc that peaks just above eye level. 50 throws.

drills.title: Scooping throw
drills.do: Throw from near the middle of your body and catch out to the side. 50 throws.

drills.title: Eyes at the peak
drills.do: Watch the top of the arc, not your hands. 50 throws.

drills.title: Rhythm
drills.do: Say 'throw' at each throw and keep the beat steady. 50 throws.

drills.title: Weak hand
drills.do: Give your weaker hand extra throws until both arcs match.

drills.title: Eyes on the wall
drills.do: 50 throws with your eyes fixed on a point on the wall.

stages.easier: Make the arc lower.
stages.harder: Toss from behind your back to the other hand.

check.task: Do 30 hand-to-hand throws in a row.
check.ready_if: 30 in a row with even arcs.

stages.title: Two balls
stages.goal: The exchange: throw the second ball when the first one peaks.

drills.title: The exchange
drills.do: One ball in each hand. Throw the right one; when it peaks, throw the left one under it. Catch both. Stop. Repeat 30 times.

drills.title: Other hand first
drills.do: The same exchange, starting with the left hand.

drills.title: Say it
drills.do: Say 'throw, throw, catch, catch' while you do exchanges.

drills.title: Even heights
drills.do: Check that both throws peak at the same height.

drills.title: Two in one hand
drills.do: Hold two balls in one hand and juggle them in that hand only, in small circles.

drills.title: Review
drills.do: 20 exchanges starting with each hand.

stages.easier: Pause longer between exchanges.
stages.harder: Do exchanges back to back without stopping.

check.task: Do 10 clean exchanges starting with each hand.

stages.title: The three-ball flash
stages.goal: Throw all three balls once and catch them all.

drills.title: Setup
drills.do: Two balls in your stronger hand, one in the other. Practice the first throw from the hand holding two.

drills.title: The flash
drills.do: Throw, throw, throw (strong, weak, strong), each when the last one peaks. Catch all three. Stop.

drills.title: Let them drop
drills.do: Do the flash and let the balls drop, just to feel the rhythm of the throws.

drills.title: Flash and catch
drills.do: Do 20 flashes, catching all three.

drills.title: Other hand first
drills.do: Do flashes starting with your weaker hand.

drills.title: Review
drills.do: Do 10 flashes starting with each hand.

stages.easier: Go back to the two-ball exchange for half the session.
stages.harder: Add a fourth throw after the flash.

check.task: Do 5 clean flashes in a row.

stages.title: The cascade
stages.goal: Keep three balls going.

drills.title: Four throws
drills.do: Do a flash and add one more throw. Then try five throws.

drills.title: Count catches
drills.do: Juggle and count catches out loud. Stop before you lose control.

drills.title: Stay in place
drills.do: If you keep walking forward to chase throws, stand facing a wall or a bed.

drills.title: Steady height
drills.do: Keep every throw at the same height, just above eye level.

drills.title: Relax
drills.do: Drop your shoulders and slow down. Slightly higher throws give you more time.

drills.title: Best run
drills.do: Try for your best run of catches.

stages.easier: Go back to the flash for half the session.
stages.harder: Juggle 10, catch them all, and start again without dropping.

check.task: Juggle your best run.

stages.title: Longer runs and control
stages.goal: Stop on purpose, recover and juggle for a minute.

drills.title: Planned stop
drills.do: Juggle and stop cleanly on a count you choose.

drills.title: Throw height
drills.do: Juggle low for 10 catches, high for 10, then back to normal.

drills.title: Recover
drills.do: When a throw goes wild, try to save it rather than stop.

drills.title: Time it
drills.do: Juggle for 30 seconds without a drop.

drills.title: Walk and juggle
drills.do: Take slow steps forward and back while juggling.

drills.title: Best run
drills.do: Try for your best run.

stages.easier: Aim for 10 catches with full control.
stages.harder: Juggle for a full minute.

check.task: Juggle your best run.

stages.title: First tricks
stages.goal: Over the top, the reverse cascade and columns.

drills.title: Over the top
drills.do: In the cascade, throw one ball over the top of the pattern instead of inside it, then carry on.

drills.title: Reverse cascade
drills.do: Throw every ball from the outside of the pattern, over the top.

drills.title: Columns
drills.do: Throw balls straight up in columns: one on each side together, then the middle one.

drills.title: Under the leg
drills.do: Throw one ball from under your leg, then go back to the cascade.

drills.title: Mix
drills.do: Cascade, one trick, cascade. Try each trick in turn.

drills.title: Show it
drills.do: Put together a 30-second routine of your tricks.

stages.easier: Learn one trick this week.
stages.harder: Chain two tricks without stopping.

check.task: Do one trick in the middle of a cascade and keep going.

speaking_topics: a meal you remember
the best advice you've been given
a place you'd like to visit
a skill you'd like to learn
how to make a good cup of tea or coffee
a small change that made your week better
why everyone should learn to cook
a book or film you'd recommend
your favorite season and why
how to plan a weekend trip
a job you'd love to try for a day
the case for walking more
something you changed your mind about
how to keep a houseplant alive
a tradition you enjoy
